speaker: Doctor
text: Please tell me your age and how long you have noticed this breast mass. Are there any other symptoms such as nipple discharge, skin changes, or pain in the affected area?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Has this mass become harder or fixed to the underlying tissue, and have you noticed any changes in the size or color of your nipples? Also, when was your last mammogram?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breast Carcinoma. Given the patient's age (48), the rapid increase in mass size, and the absence of benign features like pain or skin changes, this presentation is highly suspicious for malignancy until proven otherwise. Immediate further imaging and biopsy are required.
